v.why: Restoring the direct input-to-output path gives large gains (+6 to +48 on IN16), while replacing an existing conv or pool on edge 3 with skip gives only small gains.
Filling a missing edge 3 with a conv adds a short path and capacity at once, giving gains of 2 to 78 points, much larger than swapping one op for another on that edge.
Without edge 3, cutting edge 0 can starve or disconnect the output (-78 on C10 in one case), whereas with edge 3 present the drop is around 1 point.
Removing an output edge hurts more when the direct path to the output is already missing, because fewer routes are left to carry signal and gradients.
If edge 5 is already gone, removing edge 3 leaves edge 4 as the only output path, which makes the cell much weaker than when edge 5 still feeds the output.
A skip on edge 4 makes up for the missing edge-3 shortcut (+8.2 on IN16), but is mildly harmful when edge 3 already provides a short path (+0.35 / -1.1).
A skip on edge 5 helps deep conv cells that lack the edge-3 shortcut (+7.3 on IN16) and hurts when that shortcut exists.
Replacing the conv on edge 0 with a skip shortens the effective depth, which matters most when there is no edge-3 shortcut (+14 vs +1.6 on IN16, and positive vs negative on C10 and C100).
Adding a 3x3 conv has diminishing returns when the cell already convolves on the output edge, compared with conv-poor parents where gains are tens of points.
If edge 4 already provides a conv path through node 1, adding a conv on edge 2 adds little capacity (about 0 to 2 points) compared with conv-poor parents (+6 to +35).

I grounded these in the 98 measurements. Two patterns show up clearly:

- **Edge 3 is the key edge.** It is the direct input-to-output path. When edge 3 is `none`, the parent is badly off: adding anything on edge 3, or adding residual paths elsewhere, gives much larger gains. Removing other paths hurts more (experiments 7, 11, 12, 17, 44–48, 58–64).
- **Extra convolutions help less in conv-heavy cells.** Adding `nor_conv_3x3` gains 30–45 points in all-pool or all-skip parents but only 0–3 points when the parent already has many 3×3 convs (experiments 71–82 vs 18–26 and 95–98).

The last two hypotheses (edit edge 0 and edit edge 2 to `nor_conv_3x3`) have the weakest direct support. They rest on the second pattern rather than on matched comparisons.
